scope: Separate native rebuild, sanitizer replay, manifest verification and arithmetic recomputation. No CUDA or GPU was used.
limitations: Source word operations are not Blackwell SASS or measured throughput; the one-operation-per-lane-cycle conversion is a conditional model, not a hardware lower bound.
The same model predicts 12.844705 B/s from the 2276.25-operation reference subledger while the fused kernel measured 15.436677 B/s, so compiler lowering and overlap do not transfer exactly.
The one-word-shift diagonal count is exact only inside that abstraction; a 131-bit cross-word shift can cost more.
The greedy XOR construction is a deterministic candidate circuit, not a universal XOR lower bound.
The dynamic selector distribution is a uniform-field model; the decision uses the stronger free-selection oracle and does not depend on it.
The conclusion covers the enumerated diagonal, all-output, fixed-branch, greedy-CSE and Frobenius-composition families, not every possible GF(2) circuit.
conclusion: No enumerated construction passes the frozen conditional source-operation screen. The free-shift/free-selection oracle exceeds the 26 B/s model allowance, and its complete comparable source subledger is worse than the fused beta reference; this is not a universal circuit or hardware lower bound.
